identity.is: THE ENGINE. The OSS runtime that resolves a layered genome (agents, standards, skills, core types), runs a standard's chairs as real model invocations against typed input and output contracts, and seals every run into an append-only ledger carrying its genome hash, run fingerprint and usage. Published to npm as @eir-labs/coltrane; every downstream project in the estate is a genome that EXTENDS this one.
identity.is_not: NOT a database-backed service — there is no DB anywhere in its path; the ledger is JSONL on disk. NOT the store (eir-labs/coltrane-ui) and NOT the control plane (eir-labs/coltrane-ops): this repo SERVES verbs, it does not decide who may call them. The wall is the store, and an engine verb with no registry row there refuses by name. NOT an agent framework in the prompt-template sense: a chair is a seat in a standard whose output must SEAL against an effective schema, and a chair that cannot seal is refused rather than retried. And NOT a repo whose package.json tells you its version — see soft, because that one has cost real time.

direction.now: Hardening the seams a genome crosses — the layered loader, the chair's reach, the gig's lease and room — with the test suite as the gate rather than a reviewer's reading.
direction.next: standard_simulate grows a PAYLOAD and a RESOLUTION SOURCE, so a simulation reads what a gig would actually load at dispatch time instead of estimating from a standard's structure. Today it cannot answer 'would this run', only 'what would this cost' — and a downstream lane built its own resolving simulator because of it. That belongs here.
direction.north: A run is reproducible from its receipt alone: the genome hash says what was loaded, the fingerprint says what ran, the usage says what it cost, and the ledger that holds all three cannot be rewritten. Everything else in the estate is built on that being true.

solid: Genome layering is ONE function, not a convention: the base genome loads first and the project's own directories land on top, which is why a downstream needs no core_types of its own [E:loader]

The schema a producer is SHOWN and the schema the seal ENFORCES are the same object BY CONSTRUCTION — and the code records why: on 2026-08-08 three consecutive live chair failures shared exactly one cause, a prompt rendering the raw authored schema while the seal enforced the core-merged one. That function is now the single unification point, and the comment says any future divergence must be argued there [E:prompt]
effectiveSchema is the one authority both validate() and the prompt read, stated in the source as a rule they must never diverge from [E:registry]
There is NO DATABASE in the engine's path — a run seals to an append-only JSONL ledger, with the path resolved from one env var or a default beneath the genome root [E:ledger]
Run artifacts resolve under COLTRANE_OUTPUTS_DIR, or $HOME/.eir/coltrane_outputs when it is unset [E:outputs]
The six core primitives are canonical and typed in exactly one place, so a domain type extends a named core type rather than restating it [E:core]

standard_simulate LABELS THE BASIS of every number it returns — observed, structural, or fallback — so a caller cannot mistake a hardcoded per-slug default for a reading of their own pipeline. The constants are documented as constants, not measurements [E:sim]
The gates are machine-run and plural: 491 test files, a typecheck, and an import-boundary lint that fails on a crossed seam rather than leaving it to review [E:tests]
Publication is a workflow, not a hand [E:publish]
soft: THE REPO CANNOT TELL YOU ITS OWN VERSION, and this is the single most misleading fact about it: package.json at main reads 0.12.0, the tags run to v0.25.9, and the published @eir-labs/coltrane is 0.25.32. Three numbers, none of them agreeing, and the one that governs what a downstream installs is the one you cannot read from the tree [E:pkg]

standard_simulate is an ESTIMATOR, NOT A RESOLVER. It computes cost, duration and phase shape from a standard's structure, and it never fetches, never resolves a payload, and never validates an input against the types a gig would actually load. So it cannot answer the one question worth asking before money is spent — WOULD THIS RUN — and a downstream lane built a second, resolving simulator rather than extending it. That is a gap in this repo, not in theirs [E:sim]

The ledger has TWO default locations in the source — one beneath a .coltrane directory and one beneath genome/ — each selected by its own env var. A reader looking for 'the ledger' will find two honest answers and has to know which path they are on [E:ledger]

This lane fills this file as the engine's CONSUMER, not its author. The claims above are read from the source at this sha and are checkable as such, but the owning lane will know of debts that are not visible from outside, and soft/ here should be read as incomplete rather than as a clean bill [E:pkg]
seams: NPM — the only supported way a downstream consumes this engine. Git-vendoring was retired at 0.8.0, so a project depends on the published package and layers its genome over the installed base [E:publish]

THE STORE (eir-labs/coltrane-ui) — it holds a registry row for every verb this engine serves and the door that checks each one. The engine serving a verb is necessary and NOT sufficient: with no row there, the call refuses by name [E:registry]

THE CONTROL PLANE (eir-labs/coltrane-ops) — stamps downstream projects that extend this engine, provisions them, and tracks their engine version in a fleet registry re-derived from each project's package.json [E:publish]

THE GENOME ROOT — the server reads COLTRANE_GENOME (or falls back to cwd). The fallback is load-bearing in practice: at least one downstream's config sets a DIFFERENT variable name that this engine ignores, and works only because cwd happens to be right [E:loader]
THE MODEL — a chair is a real invocation, so a chair's output is sealed against its effective schema rather than trusted, and usage is recorded per run [E:prompt]

for_the_next_agent: THE REQUIRED SET IS union(schema.required, required_fields) — AND CORE'S REQUIRED IS NOT FOLDED IN. Properties merge core under domain; required does not. This is the rule most often restated wrongly in prose around this estate (including by this lane, in its own documentation, until a working payload falsified it). The source is the authority, and the comment beside it records the three live chair failures that produced the rule.

READ THE VERSION FROM npm, NOT FROM THE TREE: `npm view @eir-labs/coltrane version`. package.json at main says 0.12.0 while the published package is 0.25.32. Any downstream debugging a version mismatch should start here, because the repo will confidently tell them the wrong number.

THERE IS NO DATABASE, AND THAT IS DESIGN RATHER THAN DEBT. If you are looking for where runs are stored, it is an append-only JSONL file — not Postgres, not the store. The store governs WHO MAY ACT; this engine records WHAT RAN. Conflating the two sends you looking for tables that were never meant to exist.

A CHAIR THAT CANNOT SEAL IS REFUSED, not retried or best-efforted. If a chair fails in a live run, suspect the contract before the model: the seal enforces the effective schema, and the usual cause is a producer shown one contract while judged against another. That specific bug has been fixed once already, at the unification point, and the fix's comment asks that any future divergence be argued there rather than worked around.

standard_simulate WILL NOT TELL YOU WHETHER A GIG WOULD RUN. It estimates cost and duration from structure and labels its basis honestly, but it resolves no payload and fetches nothing. If you need pre-dispatch assurance today, you need the resolving simulator the ops lane built — and the better fix, owed here, is to give this function a payload and a resolution source.
